privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.draft: Draft for review before launch. It will be checked against the Data Protection Act, 2019 before SabbathLink opens to the public.

sections.p: SabbathLink helps churches in Kenya share their programmes, events and giving details with members. SabbathLink decides how the information in the app is used, and is responsible for protecting it.

Your phone number, so you can sign in. Your name, if you add it. The churches you follow. Your role, if you are a church officer. The messages we send you. Verification letters sent by people registering a church. Basic technical records needed to keep the service running and secure.

Following a church shows your religious beliefs. The Data Protection Act treats this as sensitive personal data. We use it only to run SabbathLink for you. We never sell it, and never use it for advertising.

You can see your own information. Church officers see the other officers of their church, not who follows it. SabbathLink staff can see account details to verify churches and keep the platform safe, and every time they open a person's details it is recorded. Church member rolls are never public.

We send service messages only: sign-in codes, verification, safety and account notices. They arrive in Me → Messages, and some also by SMS. You can turn SMS off there; sign-in codes still arrive. We will not send marketing without asking you first.

Our database host stores the information, currently in the European Union, with the safeguards the law requires. Our SMS provider receives your phone number to deliver texts. Neither may use it for anything else.
Until you delete your account. Records of what staff did are kept for security, but no longer point to you once your account is deleted.

You can see, correct or delete your information, and object to how it is used. To delete everything, go to Me → Delete account. You can also complain to the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC).

consent.title: Before you continue
consent.intro: SabbathLink keeps a little information about you so the app works:
points: Your phone number, to sign you in.
The churches you follow. This shows your faith, so we protect it as sensitive data and never sell it or use it for ads.
Messages we send you about your account or church.
consent.rights: You can turn SMS off or delete your account at any time in Me.
